title: Granular credit debt reconciler for preemptible/burst credits
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Problem: We observe growing divergences between the live preemptible/burst-credit ledger and downstream invoice line-items when requests were served on burst capacity or allowed to oversubscribe during autoscale spikes. Late-arriving usage events, duplicate ingest across regions, and session affinity reshuffles are contributing to 'credit debt' that is not amortized cleanly into customer invoices. This ticket implements a reconciler that computes granular debt, attaches provenance, and emits corrective adjustments to the billing pipeline with idempotent semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler runs daily and produces a per-tenant debt report with provenance pointers for >99.9% of adjustments
Adjustments are emitted as idempotent events to the billing-sink topic with a stable adjustment-id and compensating metadata
End-to-end latency (from detection to adjustment emission) for typical late-arrival windows <= 1 hour in steady state
No duplicate credits applied after re-run: safe idempotency verified on staging with replayed late events
Unit/integration tests cover late-arrival, duplicate events, cross-region shadowing, and zero-delta churn cases
proposed_solution: Introduce a 'debt reconciler' job that: 1) consumes compacted usage events and the live credit-ledger snapshot, 2) computes per-tenant debt buckets (preemptible, burst, temporary-oversubscribe), 3) applies amortization rules based on tenant plan and tenancy window, and 4) emits adjustment events with deterministic adjustment-ids. Use epochal snapshots and a watermark-driven windowing strategy to bound late arrivals. Implement a provenance map attaching source event ids and confidence scores. Leverage existing compactor infra from ENG-216412 for checkpointing and replay-safe consumption.
decisions: Use deterministic adjustment-id = sha256(tenant|window_start|bucket|source_checksum) to guarantee idempotency
Windowing strategy: primary 6-hour processing window with 24-hour late-arrival tail shaped by watermark metrics
Emit adjustments to topic billing.adjustments.v2 with schema that includes provenance pointers, confidence score, and suggested invoice tags
Perform initial runs in read-only 'report-only' mode for 2 days before enabling actual adjustments
Run reconciler as k8s CronJob with parallel shard count 32 for throughput; shard key = tenant_id % shard_count
tasks: Design API for adjustment event schema and register in schema-registry
Implement compaction consumer with watermarking and replay safety
Compute amortization rules and unit tests for plan permutations
Wire deterministic adjustment-id generation and provenance attachments
Add metrics: adjustments_emitted, adjustments_deduped, avg_latency_ms, late_arrival_tail_ratio
Run two-day report-only validation in staging and collect manual review notes
Flip to active mode and monitor customer-facing dashboards closely for 48 hours
updates: 2025-02-17: Spike completed for watermarking approach; prototype compared 3 strategies (event-time tumbling, sessionized, epochal). Chosen epochal with watermark due to lower memory and simpler backfills.
2025-02-21: API schema proposal posted to schema-registry PR 1428; some feedback from Data Infra on adding source_checksum and confidence_score fields.
2025-02-25: Implemented deterministic adjustment-id generator and unit tests (edge cases: tenant-id collisions and null window_start).

2025-03-01: Integration run in staging in report-only mode for 36 hours; uncovered two late-arrival patterns from cross-region retries that need small threshold tweak (increase watermark slack to 90s).
2025-03-04: Updated compactor checkpointing to use ENG-216412's checkpoint store and wired metrics to grafana dashboard. Preparing staging rerun with corrected watermark config.
risks: Over-eager adjustments could create customer-visible invoice noise if report-only period is bypassed
Watermark misconfiguration could either delay legitimate adjustments or apply them prematurely
Shard skew if a few tenants generate majority of late arrivals leading to hot shards
Incorrect provenance mapping could block downstream support teams from explaining adjustments to customers
rollback_plan: Run reconciler in reverse-mode that emits compensating adjustments (negating previous adjustment-id) and optionally a manual 'rollback' flag on emitted events. Keep an execution history index for 30 days to permit selective reverts by tenant and window. If compensating adjustments produce >0.5% invoice delta at threshold, pause reconciler and open incident with billing and customer success.
qa_plan: Unit tests for adjustment-id determinism, amortization rules and edgecases
Integration test using recorded late-arrival trace replay (region A and B) that asserts no duplicates after re-run
Staging run in report-only mode for 48 hours followed by manual spot auditing by PM and Billing Eng lead
Load test to simulate 10x late-arrival spike and verify shard scaling behavior
notes: Follow-up: consider adding tenant-level backfill throttle to limit invoice churn for high-velocity customers
Related: this overlaps conceptually with ENG-241000's long-tail correction framework; sync schedule with that team to avoid double adjustments
If successful, export reconciler output to console-ops for a new 'debt' tab in customer billing UI
